tasks.short: Prepare pottery for sale or exhibition and maintain networks

steps.what: Select and physically prepare the actual pottery work for sale or exhibition
inputs: Actual pottery work
Actual sale or exhibition requirements
outputs: Prepared pottery and observed condition

steps.what: Maintain actual relationships with retail, pottery, art and resource networks through personal discussion and exchange
inputs: Actual network contacts and opportunities
Prepared work and potter's aims
outputs: Human relationships and actual sale or exhibition possibilities

steps.what: Prepare the actual sale/exhibition inventory entry and check its full object description, condition, dimensions and proposed price
inputs: Actual prepared pottery and observed condition
Potter's actual measurements, description and pricing choice
Existing pottery inventory system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Complete checked sale or exhibition inventory entry

steps.what: Save the exact checked sale/exhibition inventory entry
inputs: Exact complete entry checked in s3
outputs: Saved inventory information for prepared work

tasks.design: Configure fixed object fields in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} inventory form. The potter prepares the actual work, maintains relationships and captures and checks the complete sale/exhibition entry before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated object identifiers and form layout can add effort to existing preparation records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse confirmed identifiers and fixed fields.
tasks.still_hard: Work selection, condition and trusted relationships depend on the potter.
tasks.human_edge: Present suitable work and build actual relationships with venues and retailers.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native inventory forms can reduce repeated object-field entry while physical preparation and relationships remain human.

assumptions: Conditional preparation episode with an actual existing sale/exhibition inventory entry; do not add a report to each relationship conversation or claim a measured duty mix.
Potter supplies actual measurements, description, condition and price during s1 and s3; capture and the full final check are retained. No free finished description or model-set price.
Native features first; existing equivalent forms earn zero new saving. s3 reduces fixed fields only, not measurements, artistic description or price decisions.

Save is negligible and fully retained. No catalogue publication, gallery offer, consignment agreement or follow-up message is silently performed; any actual send requires its own final-version check and separate action.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 3.8 less upkeep 1 gives net 2.8.
unknowns: Actual inventory-record practice and current native forms
research_questions: Is repeated fixed-field entry material in observed preparation episodes?

already_counted.description: Retained actual inventory capture and complete final content check

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete inventory entry checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional fixed-field saving 3.8 less upkeep 1; physical preparation and network relationships retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pack and ship pottery to retail stores or galleries

steps.what: Pack the actual pottery for the store or gallery and check physical protection and package condition
inputs: Actual pottery and packaging
Actual store or gallery shipment requirement
outputs: Packed pottery and actual package dimensions and weight

steps.what: Capture and verify the exact store/gallery address, package measurements, contents and existing shipment reference
inputs: Actual package measurements from s1
Recipient-confirmed address
Existing order and dispatch records in the pottery inventory system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked structured dispatch fields and unresolved delivery issues

steps.what: Fill the exact address-label and packing-list fields from the checked shipment data
inputs: Checked dispatch fields from s2
Existing label and packing-list template
outputs: Complete label and packing-list draft with exact shipment identifiers

steps.what: Check the complete label, packing list, matching dispatch entry and actual parcel, then attach the checked documents
inputs: Complete label and packing list from s3
Actual package and checked dispatch fields
outputs: Exact checked labelled parcel and matching dispatch entry ready for the existing carrier collection

steps.what: Hand the exact checked parcel to the existing carrier for shipment to the store or gallery
inputs: Exact parcel and documents checked in s4
Existing authorized carrier collection
outputs: Actual shipment handover outcome

steps.what: Save the exact checked dispatch entry with actual handover status
inputs: Exact dispatch entry checked in s4
Actual handover outcome from s5
outputs: Saved actual dispatch status

tasks.design: Configure native {OPS_SYSTEM} label and packing-list fields from potter-verified dispatch data. Packing stays physical, and the potter checks the complete parcel and documents before separate carrier handover and dispatch-record save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual copying into labels and packing lists can repeat checked shipment information.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse exact captured recipient and package fields.
tasks.still_hard: Protecting fragile pottery and verifying the real parcel require physical care.
tasks.human_edge: Identify unsuitable packaging and mismatches before shipment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native shipping-document templates can fill exact captured fields while fragile-goods packing and parcel checks remain human.

assumptions: Conditional shipment under an existing authorized regular carrier collection with actual manually prepared address labels and packing lists; not a measured baseline or a new carrier purchase.

Recipient supplies the address and ordinary order records identify the shipment; potter actual measurements and field capture/checking are counted in s1-s2. Missing addresses or mismatches remain manual, with no inferred delivery data.
Native templates first; existing generated labels and lists are baseline and earn zero saving. s3 replaces only manual field copying, not printing runtime, packing or document attachment.

The complete label and packing list exist before s4. Changed parcel, address or contents requires another check before handover. Any actual carrier booking or shipping-instruction send outside the existing collection must be included as its own checked action; none is silently performed here.
Handover and negligible same-system save remain fully retained. Status reflects actual handover, not assumed delivery.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross document-field transfer saving 15 less upkeep 2 gives net 13.
unknowns: Actual carrier arrangement and current label-generation features
research_questions: Which label/list fields are still copied manually after current shipping software?

already_counted.description: Actual package preparation, dispatch-data capture and complete final parcel/document verification

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete parcel, destination and documents checked in s4; any change requires recheck
Exact matching dispatch entry checked in s4 plus actual handover status only

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional manual label/list field-transfer saving 15 less upkeep 2; physical packing and actual shipment checks retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess and measure the actual display space and identify pottery, visitor and venue constraints
inputs: Actual display space and pottery
Venue's actual requirements
outputs: Potter-captured dimensions and display constraints

steps.what: Design the actual display arrangement, sight lines, object grouping and practical layout
inputs: Actual measurements and constraints from s1
Existing layout drawing tool, defined as OTHER
outputs: Potter-authored display design and selected arrangement

steps.what: Draw repeated display units and dimensions in the actual layout plan
inputs: Potter-authored layout and exact dimensions from s2
outputs: Complete editable display plan

steps.what: Check the complete final display plan against measured space, pottery and actual venue constraints
inputs: Complete plan from s3
Actual measurements and venue requirements
outputs: Exact checked display plan

steps.what: Save the exact checked display plan
inputs: Exact complete plan checked in s4
outputs: Saved display-space design

tasks.design: Configure native {OTHER} layout-tool symbols, repeats and dimensions for the potter's chosen arrangement. The potter measures, designs and checks the complete final plan before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manually drawing repeated display units can consume plan-production effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native editable symbols can reproduce explicit repeated geometry.
tasks.still_hard: Artistic presentation and physical suitability require judgement of the real space and pottery.
tasks.human_edge: Choose how the work should be seen and whether the arrangement fits its setting.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated drawing within the current display design.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native layout symbols and dimensions can reduce repeated drawing while display composition remains human design work.

assumptions: Conditional episode with an actual drawn plan and repeated display units, not measured baseline for every informal arrangement. Potter measurement and all creative design input are counted in s1-s2.
Native features first. Existing symbols earn no new saving; unsupported shapes remain manual. No free measured model or generated display concept.
s3 retains setup and geometric review. Full final checking remains in s4; save is negligible and fully retained.
This task designs the space. Physical installation, venue authorization and any external plan send must be separate checked work if actually in scope; none is silently done or credited as saving.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 7.5 less upkeep 1.5 gives net 6.
unknowns: Current drawing practice and repeated-unit effort
research_questions: Which repeated layout details are still constructed manually?

already_counted.description: Actual measurement and display design, retained drawing setup/review and complete final plan check

incremental.description: Maintain reusable display-unit symbols and dimensions

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete display plan checked in s4; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional repeated drawing saving 7.5 less upkeep 1.5; measurement and artistic design retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain pottery supplies and order replenishment

steps.what: Check actual tools, equipment and material supplies and perform existing routine upkeep
inputs: Actual tools, equipment and materials
Established workshop upkeep and stock practice
outputs: Actual condition and stock observations with routine upkeep completed

steps.what: Determine needed replenishment and capture exact selected supply identifiers, quantities and checked supplier terms
inputs: Actual stock and condition observations from s1
Supplier catalogue and prices
Existing pottery supply records, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Potter-authored structured replenishment lines and checked supplier evidence

steps.what: Stage exact selected supply identifiers and quantities into the native draft supplier order
inputs: Structured replenishment lines captured in s2
Explicit supplier item mapping
outputs: Draft replenishment order with exact-line reconciliation and unmatched items held

steps.what: Complete and check the exact final supplies order and matching internal record, including quantities, price and delivery terms
inputs: Draft order
Actual supply need and checked supplier evidence
outputs: Complete checked supplier order and matching internal record

steps.what: Submit the exact checked supply order to the supplier
inputs: Exact final order checked in s4
outputs: Submitted supply order and actual outcome

steps.what: Save the exact checked internal order record with actual submission status
inputs: Exact matching record checked in s4
Actual status from s5
outputs: Saved supplies-order record

tasks.design: Configure native draft-order imports in {PARTNER_PORTAL} from exact replenishment fields captured in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The potter retains physical stock/upkeep work and supply decisions and checks the complete order before separate submission and record save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual supplier-order entry can repeat captured replenishment lines.
tasks.enabler_now: Native draft imports can preserve exact supply identifiers and quantities.
tasks.still_hard: Actual condition, material suitability and replenishment need require workshop judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a tool or material needs attention and choose suitable supplies.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native supplier draft imports can reduce exact-line re-entry while physical stock checks and material selection remain human work.

assumptions: Conditional actual routine upkeep and manually transferred replenishment order, not a measured baseline. Potter actual observation and structured requirement capture are counted in s1-s2; no free stock feed or invented par levels.

Native features first; existing imports earn no new saving. Unmatched identifiers, proposed substitute materials and unclear quantities remain manual; no automatic substitution or equipment-control change.

Routine upkeep in s1 is ordinary non-operational tool/storage care, not machine maintenance or a hidden powered intervention. Any actual equipment-control or repair action must be separated with its specific readiness check and full effort.
Assumes actual purchasing authority for these supplies. If owner approval is required, its owner checks the complete final order before submission with their labour added.

Submission and near-zero save earn no saving. Receipt and payment remain separate existing work; no hidden purchase or bank action. If the portal already creates the internal record, no duplicate baseline is invented.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross transfer saving 25 less upkeep 3 gives net 22.
unknowns: Actual order-entry workflow and replenishment authority
research_questions: Which exact replenishment lines still require manual transfer after native supplier tools?

already_counted.description: Actual stock/upkeep work, replenishment capture and complete final supplier-order checking

incremental.description: Maintain exact supply-field mappings and validate draft-order import

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete supply order checked in s4; any item, quantity, price or term change requires recheck
Exact matching internal order record checked in s4 plus actual submission status only

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional exact-line transfer saving 25 less upkeep 3; physical maintenance, supply judgement and final actions retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
